subject.title: RFC: policy on agent-directed instruction content in docs

question: What acceptability boundary should ClawHub apply to agent-directed SKILL.md/README instructions that ask agents to fetch/run code, escalate privileges, bypass confirmation, or act outside the skill purpose?
rationale: This is a marketplace trust and security-policy choice, not a mechanical docs cleanup; current docs and scanner prompts are adjacent but do not settle the public rule or borderline cases.

options.title: Adopt a documented boundary
options.body: Approve an acceptable/needs-review/not-allowed guideline and implement it as paired spec and public docs, coordinated with the related capability and cross-asset RFCs.

options.title: Wait for adjacent RFCs first
options.body: Keep this RFC open but defer policy wording until the capability-manifest and cross-asset-signal decisions settle.

options.title: Keep case-by-case moderation
options.body: Decline a separate guideline and rely on current acceptable-use language, ClawScan review, and maintainer judgment for agent-directed instruction cases.

recommendation.title: Adopt a documented boundary
recommendation.body: Approve an acceptable/needs-review/not-allowed guideline and implement it as paired spec and public docs, coordinated with the related capability and cross-asset RFCs.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle is CODEOWNERS-listed on the central security scan paths and adjacent public security policy docs.
